profiles.title: The Don Icon of the Mother of God
profiles.subject: Theotokos

overview.text: The Don icon presents the Mother of God and Christ in a close embrace, their faces touching. The selected historical reproduction is the work traditionally associated with Theophanes the Greek, not an unrelated icon of the same saintly subjects.

blocks.text: The child turns toward Mary and raises an arm around her neck; his uncovered legs and feet are visible. Mary inclines her head while supporting him. The painted panel’s gold ground and worn surface remain visible in the reproduction.

blocks.text: The OCA attributes the icon to Theophanes the Greek and connects it with the Battle of Kulikovo in 1380. In the Church account, the Don Cossacks give it to Prince Demetrius after the victory, and he brings it to Moscow. These associations are presented as the published ecclesiastical account.

blocks.text: The same account relates the icon’s use during the threat to Moscow in 1591 and the founding of the Don Monastery in thanksgiving in 1592. It records August 19 as the icon’s feast, linking the commemoration to the city’s deliverance.
